clue.text: Barrier snaps, broken by large winged creatures

parts.note: a dam is a barrier across water

indicators.note: the snaps word is split open with the next piece set into the gap

parts.note: selfies are photographic snaps of oneself
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A barrier gets photographed by tourists while big flying insects buzz around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Damselflies are slender insects related to dragonflies, with two pairs of wings.

clue.text: I compile using such a sheet to reflect

indicators.note: a reflection shows a mirror image, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: a sheet of canvas makes a sail

explanation.surface: A setter describes making a puzzle with a sheet of paper and a mirror.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter compiles under a pen name, proXimal, so the definition is personal to them.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword compilers publish under pseudonyms, and a pseudonym is an assumed name.

clue.text: Controlled address to knight heard before offensive

indicators.note: the word is spoken aloud and written as its sound

parts.note: a knight is addressed as Sir
vile means offensive or disgusting

explanation.surface: A dominated servant addresses his knight before a nasty attack.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent SIR is said as SER; VILE is an adjective, so 'offensive' is not a military attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A servile person behaves with excessive submissiveness, as one controlled by another.

clue.text: Mortal left alien chamber diminished

indicators.note: the chamber word is made smaller by losing its last letter

parts.note: E.T. is the film alien
a hall is a large chamber or room

explanation.surface: A deadly alien abandons a shrinking chamber.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortal blow is a fatal one, so mortal and deadly share the sense of causing death.

clue.text: Ground really staying dry in recent times

indicators.note: the dry letters stay within the rearranged word
ground is the past participle of grind, so the letters are crushed into a new order

parts.note: TT stands for teetotal, a person who stays dry

explanation.surface: The ground has really stayed dry lately.
explanation.definitionFit: Latterly means lately, in the recent past, the opposite of formerly.

clue.text: Rouse some men evil nemesis upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the letters upwards so they read backwards
only some of these words' letters are used

explanation.surface: Some wicked men stir up their nemesis.
explanation.definitionFit: To enliven is to make more lively or animated, which rousing someone does.

clue.text: Power correct cables aboard ship to produce energy

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the ship letters

parts.note: SS is the steamship abbreviation
P is the physics symbol for power
right means correct
lines are cables, as telephone or power lines

explanation.surface: Electricians fix power cables on board a vessel to generate electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprightliness is liveliness and vigour, an energetic quality of a person.

clue.text: Monkey for all to see in uppermost part on projection

indicators.note: the film letter goes inside the cap and chin pair
in a down clue the cap sits on top of the chin

parts.note: a cap is the top part of something
the chin projects from the face
U is the British film rating for universal, suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: A monkey on show for everyone perches at the top of a ledge.
explanation.definitionFit: The capuchin is a small South American monkey named after the friars' hood.

clue.text: He lit some explosive with good techniques

indicators.note: an explosion blows the letters apart into a new order

explanation.surface: A demolition expert lights explosives using proven methods.
explanation.definitionFit: Methodologies are systems of methods used in a field, so they are working techniques.

clue.text: Already arranged April work, requiring no outsiders

indicators.note: each of April and work loses its outside letters, keeping only the inner ones

explanation.surface: Someone had a job booked in April before it even started, with no outside help needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A prior engagement is one fixed beforehand, so prior describes something set up in advance.

clue.text: Turn on plough, worried after it backfired

indicators.note: the plough and worried pieces come after the reversed it
something that backfires goes the wrong way, so the word it runs backwards

parts.note: to till is to plough land
ate, as in 'what's eating you?', means worried or troubled

explanation.surface: A farmer tries to start a plough, fretting after the engine backfired.
explanation.definitionFit: To titillate is to excite or arouse someone, which is the slang sense of turn on.

clue.text: Prompt search after losing case in Venice

indicators.note: the search word is wanted once it has shed the named letters

parts.note: to investigate is to search into something

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A detective is urged to search after losing a court case in Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: To instigate is to bring about or provoke an action, just as prompting sets it going.

clue.text: Pained expression after five testify

indicators.note: the pained cry comes after the numeral

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
ouch is what you say when hurt

explanation.surface: Five witnesses wince in pain before giving evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: To vouch is to give a personal guarantee or assurance, as a witness does in testimony.

clue.text: Bore cut

definitions.meaning: first meaning: bored, as in drilled or chopped a way through
second meaning: chopped roughly with blows

explanation.walkthrough: Bore reads as a noun for a tedious person, but it is the past tense of bear or bore: hacked a path through.
explanation.definitionFit: Hacking is chopping with rough blows, so the word covers both forcing a hole through and chopping something.

clue.text: Verbal agreement that's no longer up in the air

definitions.text: that's no longer up in the air
definitions.note: a definition by description: a thing that has stopped flying

indicators.note: verbal means spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: concord is harmony or agreement

explanation.surface: A spoken agreement that is no longer undecided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up in the air' looks like 'unresolved', but it means literally airborne: the supersonic airliner was retired in 2003.
explanation.definitionFit: Concorde was the supersonic passenger jet withdrawn from service, so it no longer flies.

clue.text: Drew back bolted clamps a short distance

indicators.note: the bolted word holds the next piece gripped between its letters

parts.note: to bolt is to flee, so bolted gives fled
an inch is a tiny distance

explanation.surface: Something fastened with bolts and clamps moves a little way back.
explanation.definitionFit: To flinch is to recoil or start back sharply, as from pain or fear.

clue.text: Doctor runs late — they're indifferent

definitions.note: a plural phrase for the plural answer

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered

explanation.surface: A doctor who is running late leaves patients unbothered.
explanation.definitionFit: Neutrals take no side in a conflict, so they are impartial and uncommitted.

clue.text: Artist with picture in both hands

indicators.note: the picture word sits inside the hands phrase

parts.note: the left and right hands: L and R, written L AND R
to picture is to see in the mind

explanation.surface: A painter holds his picture in both hands.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Edwin Landseer was a Victorian painter of animals who also sculpted the lions in Trafalgar Square.
explanation.definitionFit: Landseer was a famous English painter, so he is an example of an artist.

clue.text: We must abandon one of our people becoming more cruel

indicators.note: the named letters have to be dropped from the longer word

parts.note: from a Western viewpoint, one of us is a Westerner

explanation.surface: We have to desert one of our own, which turns cruel.
explanation.definitionFit: Stern means harsh and severe, so sterner is harsher, a comparative of cruelty.

clue.text: Column's put favourable slant on the French revolutionary

parts.note: to spin a story is to present it in a favourable light

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: la is French for the (feminine)

explanation.surface: A newspaper column puts a flattering slant on the French revolutionaries.
explanation.definitionFit: The spinal column is the backbone, so spinal means belonging to that column.

clue.text: Sauce and juice over most of Malaysian dish

indicators.note: in a down clue, over sends the word back up so it reads backwards

parts.note: sap is the juice of plants

indicators.note: most of the dish, its last letter dropped

parts.note: satay is a Malaysian dish of grilled skewered meat

explanation.surface: A cook pours sauce and juice over a Malaysian dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Passata is an Italian sieved tomato purée used as a base for pasta sauces.

clue.text: Costumier's opening fabric drawer

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: rayon is a synthetic fabric

explanation.surface: A costume maker opens a drawer full of fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawer' looks like a piece of furniture; it means a thing that draws.
explanation.definitionFit: A crayon is a stick of coloured wax used for drawing pictures.

clue.text: Move gingerly around old snare

indicators.note: the cautious-move word goes round the old abbreviation

parts.note: to nose forward is to move slowly and cautiously

explanation.surface: Someone creeps carefully around an old trap.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a loop of rope that tightens, used as a trap for animals.

clue.text: Hiding from abuse of human rights I'm not sure should be overlooked

indicators.note: abuse mistreats the letters of human rights, reordering them
the hesitation letters are to be left out of the mix

parts.note: um is the noise of someone unsure

explanation.surface: A report says abuses of human rights, though uncertain, should not be ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: Hiding is a noun here, a beating, not concealment. Take UM out of HUMAN RIGHTS and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiding is a severe beating, and a thrashing is the same punishment.

clue.text: Force is mile at sea outside Portugal

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go outside the country letter
at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: P is the international vehicle code for Portugal

explanation.surface: A naval force is a mile out at sea off the coast of Portugal.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or urge forward, the same as forcing someone into action.

clue.text: Headline about Prime Minister you're primarily finding unmoving

indicators.note: the headline word goes about the Prime Minister

parts.note: to headline a show is to star in it
Anthony Eden was UK Prime Minister in the 1950s

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A newspaper headline about the Prime Minister says you are stuck in place.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedentary describes a life spent sitting and inactive, with little movement.

clue.text: Generous anagram pleasantly entertains

indicators.note: the two words hold the answer within them, as a host holds guests

explanation.surface: A generous puzzle with an anagram that pleasantly amuses solvers.
explanation.definitionFit: An ample helping is a large and plentiful one, which is what a generous serving is.

clue.text: Decent clean around small desk

indicators.note: the clean word goes around the small abbreviation

parts.note: birds preen to clean their feathers
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a desk is a kind of writing table

explanation.surface: Someone tidies up round a little desk to make the room fit to be seen.
explanation.definitionFit: Presentable means fit to be seen in public, a respectable and decent appearance.
